description: The fatal READ arm of 1000-ACCTFILE-GET-NEXT at app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L92-L116, pinned from the OVER-WIDTH direction: the stored row measures 301 bytes where app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy declares 300, so the first READ at L93 reports a permanent error and the program abends without ever displaying a record. It is the mirror of case13, which pins the same arm with a row 122 bytes SHORT, and the pair exists because the guard is a width EQUALITY and not a lower bound: a decoder that read the first 300 bytes and ignored whatever followed would pass case13 and fail this one, and a decoder that padded a short row up to width would pass this one and fail case13. Neither repair is admissible, and the reason is not fastidiousness - ACCT-CURR-BAL decoded from a span that is not its own is still a number, and no caller can tell it from a real one, so a repair converts a diagnosable failure into plausible data. WHAT THE CASE DECLARES. One ACCTFILE row, so the dataset is present and 0000-ACCTFILE-OPEN succeeds at L136 with '00' - this case is about the READ and not the OPEN, which case10 and case12 pin through their absent dataset. From ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS onward the first 300 bytes are row 0 of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt verbatim, including the five zoned sign overpunches; only ACCT-ID is changed, to 00000000701, an identifier no row of that fixture carries - its keys run 00000000001 through 00000000050 - so the row can never be mistaken for one of the fifty stored records. One further byte is then appended at offset 300, the printable '!'. Printable rather than a space on purpose: a trailing space could be read as insignificant padding and argued away, and this byte cannot be. THE OFFSETS, MECHANICALLY. Zero-based offset and length over the declared 300, straight off app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy:L5-L17 rather than off prose: ACCT-ID 0/11, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS 11/1, ACCT-CURR-BAL 12/12, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT 24/12, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT 36/12, ACCT-OPEN-DATE 48/10, ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE 58/10, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE 68/10, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT 78/12, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT 90/12, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP 102/10, ACCT-GROUP-ID 112/10, FILLER 122/178 - total exactly 300, and RECLN 300 at L2 agrees. The twelve named spans sum to 122, which is precisely case13's width: the account record with its trailing FILLER PIC X(178) absent, 300 minus 178. FILLER is a span and not a comment: it is ten spaces of ACCT-GROUP-ID followed by 178 spaces of FILLER that carry offsets 112 through 299 here, and a codec that omitted FILLER would produce a 122-byte record and break every downstream offset. PIC S9(10)V99 occupies 12 bytes and not 13 - ten integer digits and two fractional ones, with no byte for the sign and none for the decimal point - the sign being carried as a zoned overpunch in the trailing byte, which is why ACCT-CURR-BAL reads 00000001940{ where '{' encodes a positive digit zero and closes the value 19.40. The five overpunched spans in this row end at zero-based offsets 23, 35, 47, 89 and 101, and every one of those bytes is '{'. Two positional facts a reader must not transpose, because a folder brief has: the 'A000000000' at offset 102 is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, and ACCT-GROUP-ID at offset 112 is ten spaces in every row of the fixture. ACCT-ADDR-ZIP is also the one named field 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD never displays - twelve named spans, eleven labelled DISPLAY lines at L119-L129, and ACCT-ADDR-ZIP is the omission - which is preserved rather than corrected. WHICH READ IS REFUSED, AND WHY IT CANNOT BE A LATER ONE. The refusal strikes READ number one, and it can strike no other. A dataset in this harness has a single record width - ParityHarness.SeededDataset measures one width and refuses a ragged row outright, because a fixed-width dataset cannot hold one - so a width refusal necessarily meets the first READ of the browse and no record block can precede it. A case that displayed three records and then met a refusal on the fourth READ is therefore not expressible for this program at all: the only mechanism that could target the Nth call at a site, a forced per-call I/O outcome, exists solely on ParityCase.ScreenRequest and is refused outright for a BATCH_JOB case, which is what every CBACT01C case must be. The retention property such a case would pin is nonetheless pinned here, at the width this arm allows: the L71 banner is emitted BEFORE the failure and the three fatal lines are emitted DURING it, and all four must survive into the fingerprint even though the run ends by throwing. An implementation that buffered SYSOUT and flushed it only on the success path would lose every one of them and would fail this case while passing case01. THE LADDER, IN SOURCE ORDER. L94 IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '00' would MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT and PERFORM 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD: not taken. L98 ELSE IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '10' would MOVE 16 TO APPL-RESULT, which satisfies the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at L63 and ends the loop silently through L108's MOVE 'Y' TO END-OF-FILE: not taken, because the status reported is not '10'. L100-L101 ELSE MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT: taken. The guard chain then fails twice - 88 APPL-AOK at L104 is false because APPL-RESULT is 12 and not 0, and 88 APPL-EOF at L107 is false because it is 12 and not 16 - so L109-L113 run in order: DISPLAY 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at L110, MOVE ACCTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L111, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L112 which emits the status line, and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at L113, which displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L170, moves 0 into TIMING at L171 and 999 into ABCODE at L172, and calls 'CEE3ABD' at L173. This is the branch a translation that treated any non-'00' status as end of data would get wrong: it would move 16 instead of 12, set END-OF-FILE, close the file and reach the closing banner with return code 0, silently converting a permanent I/O error into a clean end of file. THE RETURN CODE. 12, from the MOVE 12 at L101 and carried out by the CALL 'CEE3ABD'. Never 16, which is the APPL-EOF value; never 0; and never 999 - ABCODE 999 at L172 and TIMING 0 at L171 are Language Environment abend parameters and are not the return code. THE SECOND LINE. 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE', 26 characters, containing the word ACCOUNT. This program's three error literals are deliberately inconsistent and are reproduced exactly as they are rather than harmonised: the read literal at L110 is 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26, the open literal at L144 is the bare DD name in 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' at 22, and the close literal at L162 is 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26. case10 and case12 state the open literal; this case and case13 state the read one. THE STATUS LINE, DERIVED. 01 IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at L57-L59, four bytes in total, and both arms of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS display the 20-character literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' and then that image, so the line is 24 characters and the NNNN is part of the hard-coded literal at L183 and L187 rather than a placeholder awaiting substitution. The numeric ELSE arm at L184-L187 runs when IO-STATUS is numeric and IO-STAT1 is not '9': MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which overlays the third and fourth bytes only - so on a mainframe a VSAM record-not-found status of '23' has IO-STAT1 '2', which is numeric and is not '9', takes that arm and renders 0, 0, 2, 3 for FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0023, and a permanent I/O error of '30' renders NNNN0030 the same way. Neither is what this translation can report. The IF arm at L177-L183 runs instead when IO-STATUS is not numeric or IO-STAT1 is '9': it moves IO-STAT1 into IO-STATUS-04(1:1) and the unsigned binary value of IO-STAT2 into IO-STATUS-0403. This migration reaches its data through a configuration-bound JDBC driver whose refusal carries no VSAM feedback code to report, so AccountRepository reports PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS - '9' followed by a binary-zero feedback byte - for a row whose fields it will not decode, that status takes the IF arm, and it renders 9 then 000: FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000, also 24 characters. The frozen contract fixes that value rather than leaving it to a case: FileStatus declares no '23' and no '30' at all, and CBACT01CParityTest requires every case whose return code is not zero to end with the rendering composed from AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS followed by 'ABENDING PROGRAM'. This case therefore states 9000 and records the divergence here rather than resolving it silently, the same treatment case13 gives 0030 and case10 gives 0035. Nothing the case pins depends on the four-character image: the arm reached, the literal displayed, the guard chain that fails twice and the return code 12 are identical either way. NOTHING BEFORE AND NOTHING AFTER. No labelled field line, no 49-dash separator and no 300-byte record image appears anywhere in SYSOUT, because the first READ never yielded a decodable record. A successful read would have produced thirteen lines and in this order: the eleven labelled lines and the separator from 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD, which is performed at L96 from INSIDE the read paragraph, and then the mainline's raw DISPLAY ACCOUNT-RECORD at L78 - the same record displayed twice, once field by field and once as its 300 stored bytes, which is a quirk of the source and not a duplication to be tidied away. Nothing follows the abend either: L173 terminates the program, so 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE at L83 is never performed, no 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' line can appear, and the closing banner at L85 is never reached. SYSOUT is exactly these four lines, of 38, 26, 24 and 16 characters. WHAT IS NOT EXPECTED, AND WHY THAT IS ITSELF AN ASSERTION. "expectedWrites" is empty and says positively that nothing was written: CBACT01C opens the dataset INPUT and issues no WRITE and no REWRITE at all - the name AccountBalanceJob notwithstanding, it computes no balance and updates nothing. "expectedFinalState" is empty because a 301-byte row has no 300-byte layout to be described by, and describing it under one would be a false statement about its bytes rather than an assertion about them; this run's behaviour shows in the displayed line sequence and the return code instead. No "normalisations" is declared, because acctdata is already at its copybook width - only cardxref, short of CVACT03Y by its FILLER PIC X(14), and USRSEC, short of CSUSR01Y by its SEC-USR-FILLER PIC X(23), need one. No job parameter is declared, because app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT01C with no PARM. DETERMINISM, CODE PAGE AND NAMING. The case is deterministic: the condition it forces is a fixed literal row width, and it carries no wall-clock value and no random value. Every byte of the seeded row and of every expected line is US-ASCII, the code page of app/data/ASCII and of ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET, and never a platform default - a space is 0x20 there and 0x40 under IBM037, so the code page changes the bytes. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key, ACCTFILE, which is the DD name at app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L25; no fully-qualified dataset name appears here, because those live only in application.yml. ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the misspelling app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy:L11 gives it, because the field name is part of the contract that field-for-field diffing compares on and renaming it would silently break that comparison. PROVENANCE. Statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, app/jcl/READACCT.jcl and app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, cross-checked against the constants published by AccountBalanceJob, AccountRepository, AbendException and FileStatus. Nothing here was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a run of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L173 - and that substitution of provenance, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A.
